en: The Scripture Spoken by the Buddha on the Joyful Horripilation of the Body,
Volume One. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master of the Tang Dynasty, Chao-san-dafu, Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial,
Great Master of Pristine Dharma, Imperially Enfeoffed Purple-Robed Śramaṇa, Subject Weijing, and others.
Translated by Imperial Decree. Thus have I heard:
At one time, the World-Honored One was staying in the city of Vaiśālī, in the most excellent Great City, within the most excellent forest, together with a community of bhikṣus.

At that time, there was a son of a householder in that city named Sunakṣatra, who had recently renounced the Buddha-dharma. Not long after his departure, he slandered the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha for various reasons, saying:
"The śramaṇa Gautama!..."
Since there is not yet even the supreme Dharma among men, how much less could there be the realization of the most excellent noble knowledge and vision?

To enter into such debate, he acts as a śrāvaka, proclaiming various dharmas; that which he seeks and cultivates is realized through his own sophistry and incorrect wisdom. How could the Dharma he teaches be able to provide the essential departure that brings an end to suffering?

At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra, having dressed and taken his bowl at the hour of eating, entered the great city of Vaiśālī to beg for alms in sequence, and heard that the elder’s son Sunakṣatra was slandering the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha through various means.

Then, having completed his almsround, the Venerable Śāriputra returned to his original place; after finishing his meal, he put away his robe and bowl, washed both feet, and went to where the Buddha was. Prostrating with his head at the ground, he paid homage at the World-Honored One’s feet, withdrew to sit to one side, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!”

Today, as I entered the great city of Vaiśālī to beg for alms, I heard that the elder’s son Sunakṣatra within that city was slandering the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha through various means, saying:
"The śramaṇa Gautama!..."
Since there is not yet even the supreme Dharma among men, how much less could that which is realized through the most excellent noble knowledge and vision enter into debate?

Being merely a śrāvaka, he proclaims various dharmas; what he seeks and cultivates is realized through his own dialectical skill and incorrect wisdom. How could the Dharma he teaches be able to provide the essential departure that brings an end to suffering?
“World-Honored One!
That son of a householder has only recently departed from the Buddha-dharma; for what reason does he speak such words?
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Venerable Śāriputra, saying:

"You should know now that the elder's son, Sunakṣatra, is extremely coarse and evil; he conceals his own transgressions, and because of this concealment, he slanders the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha, uttering such words."
"Śāriputra! As you have heard, that son of a householder uttered words contrary to the Dharma as a slander, saying:
'The śramaṇa Gautama!'"
"Could the various dharmas taught by him for the sake of the śrāvakas truly provide the essential escape that reaches the ultimate end of suffering?
Listen well; I shall now briefly explain this matter to you.
Śāriputra! That son of a householder lacks the seed of faith within my Dharma.

[He does not recognize] the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavān—one who is fully endowed with these ten titles.
Although that son of a householder knew and saw these matters, because of his lack of faith, he spoke these words:
"The śramaṇa Gautama!"
There is not yet even the supreme dharma among men, much less the realization of the most excellent noble knowledge and vision; they have entered into contentious debate.
For the sake of the śrāvakas, they proclaim various dharmas, and that which they seek and cultivate is realized through their own dialectical skill and incorrect wisdom.
"Because of those thoughts, words, and views, and because they have continuously slandered [the Dharma], they will swiftly fall into hell as if dropping a heavy burden. Furthermore,

just as a śrāvaka bhikṣu who is fully endowed with the training in ethical discipline, concentration, and wisdom attains the realization of the fruit through little exertion without finding it difficult,
so too is it for them as they fall into the evil destinies!"
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!
That son of a householder lacks the seed of faith within my Dharma.

Regarding all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas who dwell, sit, or lie in forest hermitages (araṇya), far removed from the various clamors of the marketplace and the necessities for housing and bedding used by people, he has likewise cast them all aside."
Although that son of a householder knew and saw these matters as such, because of his lack of faith, he uttered these words and engaged in slander.
Because they continuously slander based on those thoughts, words, and perceptions, they will swiftly fall into hell.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra,
that son of a householder lacks the seed of faith within my Dharma."

All Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, having become detached from desire and free from evil, having stilled unwholesome states, with directed thought and evaluation, and with the joy and happiness born of seclusion, realize the first dhyāna.
Although that son of a householder knew and saw these matters as they were, because of his lack of faith, he uttered such words and engaged in slander.
Due to the continuity of that mental state, speech, and vision of slander, he will swiftly fall into hell.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!
That son of a householder does not possess the seed of faith within my Dharma.

All Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, having stilled vitarka and vicāra, with internal and external purity, one-pointedness of mind, free from vitarka and vicāra, and possessing the joy and bliss born of concentration, realize the second dhyāna."
Although that son of a householder knew and saw such matters as these, because of his lack of faith, he uttered these words and engaged in slander.
Because they continuously slander based on those thoughts, words, and perceptions, they will swiftly fall into hell.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra,
that son of a householder lacks the seed of faith within my Dharma."

All Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, being free from the craving for joy, through right knowledge as it truly is, cultivate the practice of equanimity and mindfulness; they experience sublime bliss with the body, free from the perception of craving, and—just as the noble ones observe—the practice of equanimity and mindfulness, they realize the third dhyāna, which is sublime bliss free from joy.
Although that son of a householder knew and saw such matters, because of his lack of faith, he uttered these words and slandered [the teaching].
Because they continuously slander through such thoughts, words, and perceptions, they will swiftly fall into hell.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra,
that son of a householder lacks the seed of faith within my Dharma."

All Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas have completely severed both suffering and pleasure; they are free from the two types of phenomena—the agreeable and the disagreeable—that previously existed; having removed perceptions of suffering and pleasure, their equanimity and mindfulness are purified, and they realize the fourth dhyāna.
Although that son of a householder knew and saw these matters as they were, because of his lack of faith, he uttered such words and engaged in slander.
Because they continuously slander based on those thoughts, words, and what they have seen, they will swiftly fall into hell.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra,
that son of a householder lacks the seed of faith within my Dharma."

All Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas transcend all perceptions of form, leave behind the resistance of conceptualizations, do not direct their attention toward diverse perceptions, and taking infinite space as their object of focus, realize the meditative absorption of the Sphere of Infinite Space.
Although that son of a householder knew and saw such matters as these, because of his lack of faith, he uttered these words and engaged in slander.
Because they continuously slander that mind, those words, and what was seen by him, they will swiftly fall into hell.
It is the same for the other realizations and the nine successive meditative attainments!
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!
That son of a householder lacks the seed of faith within my Dharma.
Regarding all that which is possible and impossible, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha knows it all as it truly is through his own power of wisdom."
The Tathāgata has attained such power of wisdom; yet that son of a householder, although he knows and sees these matters, speaks these words out of lack of faith, thereby engaging in slander.
Because they continuously slander based on those thoughts, words, and what they have seen, they will swiftly fall into hell.
Furthermore, Śāriputra,
that son of a householder lacks the seed of faith within my Dharma.
All Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas fully and truly understand, through right wisdom, all the paths traversed and reached by them.

The Tathāgata has accomplished such power of wisdom; yet that son of a householder, although he knows and sees this matter as it is, because of his lack of faith, utters these words and thereby slanders me.
Because they continuously slander based on those thoughts, words, and perceptions, they will swiftly fall into hell.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra,
that son of a householder lacks the seed of faith within my Dharma."
All Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, throughout various realms and innumerable worlds, fully and truly understand all things through right wisdom.
The Tathāgata has accomplished such power of wisdom; although that son of a householder knows and sees these matters, because he does not believe, he utters these words and engages in slander.
Because they continuously slander based on those thoughts, words, and what they have seen, they will swiftly fall into hell.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra,
that son of a householder lacks the seed of faith within my Dharma."

All Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, regarding all sentient beings and their countless various inclinations and understandings, weigh them all with right knowledge and comprehend each one exactly as it is.
The Tathāgata has attained such power of wisdom; yet that son of a householder, although he knows and sees these matters, speaks these words out of lack of faith, thereby engaging in slander.
Because of those thoughts and words, and because he continued to slander what he had seen, he will quickly fall into hell.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra,
that son of a householder has not planted the seed of faith within my Dharma."
All Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, regarding the various faculties of all sentient beings, weigh them all with right wisdom and understand each one exactly as it is.
The Tathāgata has accomplished such power of knowledge; yet that son of a householder, although he knows and sees this matter, speaks these words out of lack of faith, thereby engaging in slander.
Because they continuously slander based on those thoughts, words, and what they have seen, they will swiftly fall into hell.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra,
that son of a householder lacks the seed of faith within my Dharma."

All Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, regarding all sentient beings, weigh and measure their accumulated karmas as well as their lifespans with right wisdom, knowing each one exactly as it is.
The Tathāgata has accomplished such power of wisdom; yet that son of a householder, although he knows and sees these matters, speaks thus out of lack of faith, thereby engaging in slander.
Because they continuously slander based on those thoughts, words, and perceptions, they will swiftly fall into hell.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra,
that son of a householder lacks the seed of faith within my Dharma."

All Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, through right wisdom, know as they truly are all meditative concentrations, liberations, samādhis, and samāpattis, arising from both defilement and purity.
The Tathāgata has accomplished such power of wisdom; yet that son of a householder, although he knows and sees this, because of his lack of faith, utters these words and thereby slanders me.
Because they continuously slander based on those thoughts, words, and what they have seen, they will swiftly fall into hell.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra,
that son of a householder lacks the seed of faith within my Dharma."

All Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, with the pure divine eye that surpasses the human eye, are able to observe the birth and death, the beautiful and the ugly, the noble and the lowly, of all sentient beings in the world, according to what they receive through their karma.

If sentient beings, through body, speech, and mind, commit unwholesome deeds, revile the noble ones, and give rise to false views, they will, by virtue of accumulating such karma of false views, at the dissolution of the body after death, fall into the miserable realms and be born in the hells.

If sentient beings, through body, speech, and mind, perform various wholesome deeds, do not revile the noble ones, and give rise to right views, they will, by virtue of accumulating such karma of right views, at the dissolution of the body after death, be born in the happy realms within the celestial worlds.
By means of his divine eye and correct wisdom, the Tathāgata sees and knows all things.
Having accomplished such power of wisdom, although that son of a householder knew and saw these matters, because of his lack of faith, he uttered these words as a slander.
Because they continuously slander based on those thoughts, words, and what they have seen, they will swiftly fall into hell.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra,
that son of a householder lacks the seed of faith within my Dharma."

All Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas possess the power of knowledge consisting of the recollection of various former abodes; that is to say, they are able to know one birth, two births, three, four, or five births, or ten, twenty, up to a hundred births, a thousand births, a hundred thousand births, and even countless hundreds of thousands of births.

Among all beings, whether in the process of formation or destruction, he perceives all matters concerning the kalpas of formation and destruction: their former surnames, names, lineages, physical appearances, food and drink, lifespans, and experiences of suffering and pleasure; how they died here to be born there, and how they died there to be born here.
All such matters as these, he contemplates with correct wisdom exactly as they are, understanding each one clearly.
The Tathāgata has accomplished such power of wisdom; yet that son of a householder, although he knows and sees these things, because of his lack of faith, utters these words and thus slanders me.
Because they continuously slander based on those thoughts, words, and what they have seen, they will swiftly fall into hell.
Furthermore, Śāriputra,
that son of a householder lacks the seed of faith within my Dharma.
All Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas have exhausted all outflows; they are no longer subject to the increase of outflows; their minds are well-liberated and their wisdom is well-liberated.
Regarding such dharmas, he has accomplished what was to be realized through his own supernormal powers.

Śāriputra, although the Tathāgata is fully endowed with these ten powers, and although that son of a householder knows and sees these matters, because of his lack of faith, he utters these words and thus engages in slander.
Because they continuously slander based on those thoughts, words, and what they have seen, they will swiftly fall into hell.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra,
that son of a householder lacks the seed of faith within my Dharma."

All Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, having accomplished the four fearlessnesses, fully know the sphere of the noble ones; amidst the great assembly, they roar the lion’s roar and turn the Great Brahma-wheel, which no other śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas, Māras, or Brahmas can ever turn.

What are the four? First, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, having realized all-knowledge, knows all things—this dharma and that dharma—without exception. In the midst of the great assembly, he speaks these words: "I have attained peace, happiness, fearlessness, and intrepidity;

I have realized, as it truly is, the sphere of the noble ones' conduct. I let out the lion's roar and turn the Great Brahma Wheel, which others cannot turn. I do not see any śramaṇa, brāhmaṇa, deva, māra, or Brahmā who is my equal."
"Second, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, whose outflows are exhausted, speaks thus in the midst of the great assembly:

'I have attained peace and happiness, free from fear and dread; having realized as it truly is the sphere of the noble ones, I roar the lion's roar and turn the Great Brahma Wheel, which others cannot turn. I do not see any śramaṇa, brāhmaṇa, deva, māra, or Brahmā who is my equal.'"

"Third, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, for the sake of those śrāvakas who practice in accordance with the Dharma, proclaims the practice to be cultivated and the conduct to be followed, as previously explained at length. Regarding the supreme realization, amidst the great assembly, he speaks these words:

'I declare that sensual desire is a dharma that obstructs the Path. Having attained peace, joy, fearlessness, and intrepidity, and having realized the sphere of the noble ones as it truly is, I let out the lion's roar and turn the Great Brahma-wheel, which others cannot turn. I do not see any śramaṇa, brāhmaṇa, deva, Māra, Brahmā, or anyone else who is my equal.'"

"Fourth, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, for the sake of his śrāvakas, teaches the Dharma of the Noble Path, which is able to lead to liberation and bring an end to suffering. In the midst of the great assembly, he speaks thus:

'I have attained peace and bliss, free from fear and dread; having realized, as it truly is, the sphere of the noble ones, I roar the lion’s roar and turn the Great Brahma Wheel, which no one else can turn. I do not see any śramaṇa, brāhmaṇa, deva, māra, or Brahmā who is my equal.'"

“Śāriputra! The Tathāgata is fully endowed with these four kinds of fearlessness. Although that son of a householder knows and sees such matters, because he lacks faith, he utters these words to engage in slander.”
Because they continuously slander based on those thoughts, words, and views, they will swiftly fall into hell.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra,
there are eight assemblies in the world."

What are the eight? First, the assembly of kṣatriyas; second, the assembly of brāhmaṇas; third, the assembly of householders; fourth, the assembly of śramaṇas; fifth, the assembly of the gods of the Four Great Kings; sixth, the assembly of the Trāyastriṃśa gods; seventh, the assembly of Māra; and eighth, the assembly of Brahmā gods.

“Śāriputra! In the past, I have gone to countless hundreds of thousands of assemblies of kṣatriyas; according to whatever physical appearance those assemblies possessed, I likewise manifested that same form.
According to the extent of the radiance of those assemblies, I likewise possessed that same radiance.”
Those assemblies may expound the Dharma according to their own teachings; I shall first conform to what they say, and only thereafter will I speak of the Dharma that surpasses theirs.
Although I speak in this manner, those assemblies will still be unable to understand or comprehend it. For this reason, those assemblies will harbor doubts, thinking:
"Is the Dharma just spoken by this śramaṇa [the same as ours]?"
"Was it spoken by a brahmin?
Or was it spoken by a deva, a human, Māra, or Brahmā?
At that time, I further expounded the supreme Dharma for him, instructing, exhorting, benefiting, and gladdening him.
Having instructed, exhorted, benefited, and gladdened them as was appropriate, I then made my body invisible.
Although I thus concealed my physical form, that assembly was entirely unable to perceive it, and they again gave rise to this doubt:
"Was that which just vanished a śramaṇa?"
"Is it a brahmin? Or is it a deva, a human, Māra, or Brahmā?
"Śāriputra! [the Buddha said.]
At that time, I manifested my own physical form to be equal to theirs; yet even those in the assembly were still unable to see me, let alone one who surpasses me.
The supreme Dharma spoken at that time was what is known as the most excellent divine knowledge and vision.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

In the past, I have gone to the assemblies of countless hundreds of thousands of brahmins; according to whatever physical appearance those assemblies possessed, I likewise manifested that same form and appearance;
according to the extent of the radiance of those assemblies, I likewise possessed that same manifestation of light."
Those assemblies may expound the Dharma according to their own teachings; I shall first conform to what they say, and only thereafter will I speak of the Dharma that surpasses theirs.
Although I speak in this manner, those assemblies are entirely unable to understand or comprehend it. For this reason, those assemblies harbor doubts, thinking:
"Is the Dharma just spoken the teaching of a śramaṇa?"
"Was it spoken by a brahmin?
Or was it spoken by a deva, a human, Māra, or Brahmā?
At that time, I further expounded the supreme Dharma for him, instructing, teaching, benefiting, and gladdening him.
Having instructed, exhorted, benefited, and gladdened them as was appropriate, I then made my body invisible.
Although I thus concealed my physical form, that assembly was entirely unable to perceive it, and they again gave rise to this doubt:
"Was that which has just vanished a śramaṇa?"
“Is it a brahmin? Or is it a deva, a human, a Māra, or a Brahmā? Śāriputra!
At that time, I manifested my own physical form to be equal to theirs; yet even that assembly was still unable to see me, let alone one who surpasses me.

As for the supreme Dharma spoken at that time—namely, the most excellent divine knowledge and vision—it was likewise so for the other elders, śramaṇas, the gods of the Four Great Kings, the Trāyastriṃśa gods, and the hosts of Māra.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

In the past, I have gone to the assemblies of countless hundreds of thousands of Brahmās; according to whatever physical appearance those assemblies possessed, I likewise manifested that same form and appearance;
according to the extent of the radiance of those assemblies, I likewise possessed that same radiance."
Those assemblies may expound the Dharma according to their own teachings; I shall first conform to what they say, and only thereafter will I speak of the Dharma that surpasses theirs.
Although I speak in this manner, those assemblies will still be unable to understand or comprehend it. For this reason, those assemblies will harbor doubts, thinking:
"Is the Dharma just spoken by this śramaṇa [the same as ours]?"
"Was it spoken by a brahmin?
Or was it spoken by a deva, a human, Māra, or Brahmā?
At that time, I further expounded the supreme Dharma for him, instructing, encouraging, benefiting, and gladdening him.
Having thus instructed, exhorted, benefited, and gladdened them as was appropriate, I then made my body invisible.
Although I had thus concealed my physical form, that assembly was entirely unable to perceive it, and they again gave rise to this doubt:
"Was that which has just vanished a śramaṇa?"
"Is it a brahmin? Or is it a deva, a human, Māra, or Brahmā? Śāriputra!
At that time, I manifested my own physical form so as to be equal to theirs; yet even those assemblies were still unable to see me, let alone one who surpasses me.
The most supreme Dharma spoken at that time was what is called the most excellent divine knowledge and vision.
“Śāriputra! Although that son of a householder knows and sees such matters as these, because he lacks faith, he utters these words and engages in slander.”
Because they continuously slander based on those thoughts, words, and perceptions, they will swiftly fall into hell.

Furthermore, Śāriputra, regarding the paths leading to the hells, the karmic causes for rebirth there, and even the retributions experienced by sentient beings— I know each and every one of these exactly as they are.
Furthermore, he knows as they truly are the paths traversed by animals, the karmic causes leading to those destinies, and even the retributions experienced by sentient beings therein;
he likewise knows as they truly are the paths traversed by hungry ghosts, the karmic causes leading to those destinies, and even the retributions experienced by sentient beings therein;

and he knows as they truly are all the paths of the asuras, the paths of humans, and the paths of devas, the karmic causes leading to those destinies, and even the specific retributions experienced by each and every sentient being therein.
Śāriputra! As for the noble path practiced for the sake of nirvāṇa, the dharmas of nirvāṇa, and even the fruit of nirvāṇa realized by sentient beings—he knows them all as they truly are.
Śāriputra! Although that son of a householder knew and saw such matters, because of his lack of faith, he uttered these words to slander them.
Because they slander [the Dharma] through their thoughts, words, and what they perceive, and because they persist in such [false views], they will swiftly fall into hell.
